methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A community-led initiative to evaluate AI readiness in Roanoke Valley signals grassroots capacity-building beyond traditional tech hubs, potentially distributing deep AI fluency through peer networks rather than waiting for platform solutions.

signals.title: Norfolk prosecutors partner with Harvard to test new AI tool - WHRO
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk prosecutors partnering with Harvard on AI tools demonstrates deep technical engagement in Hampton Roads, but the elite academic partnership model suggests concentrated expertise rather than distributed community capability.

signals.title: Some Southwest Virginia localities look to zoning to slow down data centers
signals.signal_reading: Local governments in Southwest Virginia passing defensive zoning against data centers reveals communities experiencing AI infrastructure as extractive rather than capacity-building, signaling neither depth nor meaningful distribution of AI benefits.

signals.title: Amazon pledges millions to cover in-demand career training at Virginia community colleges
signals.signal_reading: Amazon funding community college career training creates broad access to AI-adjacent workforce skills, but corporate platform delivery model suggests shallow, employer-defined adoption rather than deep community-owned capability.

signals.title: Norfolk, Newport News police launch AI tool for non-emergency calls - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk and Newport News deploying turnkey AI call systems represents shallow platform adoption—operational efficiency gains without building local AI development capacity or transferable technical expertise.
